access_links.label: Loon blog: Turning on Project Loon in Puerto Rico

dedupe_keys.name: project loon balloon connectivity in puerto rico after hurricane maria 2017

description: This emergency-response case describes the use of stratospheric balloons to restore basic mobile service in Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria struck on 20 September 2017 and put about 95 per cent of the island's cell sites out of service. The Federal Communications Commission granted Alphabet's Project Loon an experimental licence on 7 October 2017 to operate up to 30 balloons; launched from Nevada and steered by machine-learning navigation to cluster over the island, the balloons acted as floating LTE base stations connected to ground stations and carried traffic for AT&T and later T-Mobile customers, giving text messaging, email and basic web access. Loon reported that more than 100,000 people had been connected by early November 2017, before the service ended as terrestrial networks were rebuilt, which took about half a year for most cell sites. Coverage: Puerto Rico, October to December 2017. Format and access: free blog posts by Loon's head and news reports; the FCC licence is on the FCC experimental licensing system. Caveats: user numbers are the operator's own; performance data were not published; Loon itself closed in 2021. Simulation uses: emergency response options for restoring connectivity when terrestrial networks fail, recovery and restoration timelines for mobile networks after hurricanes, and capacity of aerial platforms. Related records: the GAO report on Hurricane Maria telecom restoration and the FCC 2017 hurricane season review describe the terrestrial side, and the FCC Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative followed later.
